task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm hoping you can help me out. For the past few hours I haven't been able to send picture messages — you know, MMS — from my messaging app. Regular texts seem to go through fine, but anything with a photo just sits there and won't send. It's been pretty frustrating.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry you're running into that — MMS issues can definitely be frustrating. Let me take a look at your account first so I can check on your line.

Could you please provide the phone number on the line that's having trouble (or your full name and date of birth for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure thing! My name is John Smith, and the phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
I've found your account, John. Good news — I can see the likely cause already.

Your line 555-123-2002 is on the Premium Plan with a **15.0 GB** data limit, and you've used **15.1 GB** this cycle. Your data is essentially maxed out, which cuts off data connectivity — and MMS (picture messaging) requires mobile data to work. That's also why your plain SMS texts still go through; those don't need data.

To get picture messaging working again, we can add more data to your line. Your plan's rate is **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum I can add is **2 GB**.

How much data would you like me to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh, that makes sense actually — I didn't realize picture messages needed data. That would explain why my regular texts are fine.

Before you add it, can you just confirm this won't change my actual plan? I don't want to switch plans or anything, just top up the data. If it's just a one-time add-on, then let's go ahead with the full 2 GB.

turns.thought:
Confirmed — this is a **one-time data add-on only**. It does not change your plan, your monthly price ($65.00/month for Premium Plan), or your contract. The $4.00 for 2 GB will simply be added as a charge to your current bill.

Let me apply the 2 GB to line 555-123-2002 now.

- **Added:** 2 GB to line 555-123-2002
- **Charge:** $4.00, added to your current bill
- **Remaining data this cycle:** 2.0 GB of refueled data available

A couple of things to try now:
1. **Open your messaging app and try sending that picture message again** — it should go through now that data connectivity is restored. If any messages are still stuck in your outbox, you may need to tap and resend them.
2. If it still doesn't send, a quick reboot of your phone can help refresh the connection.

Your billing cycle resets on **2025-02-28**, at which point you'll get your full 15 GB again.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

turns.thought:
I understand — that is frustrating. Let's dig into a few other common causes of MMS problems. The data limit was only one possibility, so let's check your phone's settings directly.

Could you please check the following on your device:

1. **Check your status bar** — look at the icons at the top of your screen. Do you see a signal strength indicator (bars) and a network type like "5G", "LTE", or "4G"? If so, what does it show?
2. **Check your APN settings** — this is the technical setting your phone uses to connect to data and picture messaging. Is it showing as correct, and is there an MMSC URL listed?

Let me know what you see and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check both of those for you.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's very likely the real problem now. Your APN settings and MMSC URL look correct, so those are fine. But **"No Signal"** and **"Data Disabled"** mean your phone isn't connected to the cellular network at all, and mobile data is switched off. Without service, MMS can't send — and that's independent of the data top-up we did.

Let's work through this. Please do these checks and let me know the results:

1. **Check your network status** — this tells us whether Airplane Mode is on, your signal strength, network type, and whether mobile data and data roaming are enabled. (Specifically, let me know if Airplane Mode shows as ON.)
2. **Check your SIM status** — this shows whether your SIM is active, missing, or locked.
3. **Check your Wi-Fi calling status** — let me know whether Wi-Fi Calling is ON or OFF.

Go ahead and run those three and tell me what each one says — then I'll walk you through the right fix.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me run those three checks now.

turns.thought:
That's the key finding — yes. **"No SIM card detected"** is the root cause. Your phone can't connect to the cellular network at all without the SIM, which is why you're seeing "No Signal" and "no service." The Mobile Data "disabled" and Wi-Fi radio off are just symptoms of that, and MMS can't send without cellular service. (Your APN and MMSC URL look correct, so we don't need to touch those.)

Let's try the most common fix — reseating the SIM card:

**Please use the "Reseat SIM Card" action on your phone.** This simulates removing and reinserting the SIM, which clears up most recognition problems.

Once you've done that:
1. **Check your SIM status again** — let me know if it now says "Active."
2. **Check your network status** — see if signal bars and a network type (5G/LTE/4G) have returned.

Two notes while we're at it:
- Your **Wi-Fi Calling is ON**, and your Wi-Fi radio is currently off. Wi-Fi Calling can sometimes interfere with MMS depending on carrier support, so we may want to turn that OFF as a next step. We'll do that after we confirm your SIM is being read.
- If your SIM status still shows missing/locked after reseating, tell me and I'll take it from there.

Go ahead and reseat the SIM, and let me know what the two checks report.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me try reseating the SIM card.

turns.thought:
Great progress! The SIM reseat worked — you now have a cellular connection. Two things are still blocking MMS, though:

1. **Mobile Data is disabled** — MMS requires it.
2. **You're on a 2G network** — 2G is generally not suitable for MMS, and it explains the poor signal/speed.

Let's fix both. Please do these on your device:

**Step 1: Turn mobile data ON**
- Use the **"Toggle Data"** action to turn Mobile Data **ON**.

**Step 2: Change your network mode preference**
- First, use **"Check Network Mode Preference"** to see what your phone is currently set to.
- If it shows **2G** or **3G**, use **"Set Network Mode Preference"** and set it to **`4g_5g_preferred`**. This lets your phone connect to 4G/5G, which is faster and supports picture messaging.

**Step 3: Turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF**
- Your Wi-Fi Calling is currently **ON**, and your Wi-Fi radio is off. Wi-Fi Calling can conflict with MMS depending on carrier support, so use **"Toggle Wi-Fi Calling"** to turn it **OFF**.

Once you've done all three, please run:
- **"Run Speed Test"** — to confirm you have an actual data connection now.
- **"Can Send MMS"** — to see if picture messaging is working.

Let me know what those report and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps for me to do at once — I can only really handle one action at a time on my end, so could you walk me through them one by one? Which one would you like me to do first?

turns.thought:
Absolutely — of course, one at a time. Let's start with the simplest and most important one:

**Step 1: Turn Mobile Data ON**

Please use the **"Toggle Data"** action on your phone to turn Mobile Data **ON**.

MMS needs mobile data to send pictures, so this is the most likely remaining blocker. Once you've done it, just let me know what it reports back — no need to check anything else right now. We'll take the next step after that.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning mobile data on now.

turns.thought:
Good — data is on. Now let's fix that 2G connection, since 2G generally can't handle picture messaging.

**Step 2: Change your network mode preference**

Please use the **"Set Network Mode Preference"** action and set the mode to **`4g_5g_preferred`**.

This tells your phone to prefer 4G and 5G networks instead of sticking with 2G, which should give you a stronger signal and a fast enough connection for MMS.

Once you've set it, let me know what it reports back.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, setting the network mode preference to 4G/5G preferred now.

turns.thought:
Excellent! Signal and network type are now good. Let's clear the last potential blocker:

**Step 3: Turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF**

Please use the **"Toggle Wi-Fi Calling"** action to turn Wi-Fi Calling **OFF**.

Your Wi-Fi Calling is currently ON, but your Wi-Fi radio is off. In some cases, Wi-Fi Calling configuration can interfere with MMS depending on carrier support, so let's switch it off for now.

Once you've done that, let me know what it reports. Then I'll have you run a final check to confirm picture messaging is working.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning Wi-Fi Calling off now.

turns.thought:
All the settings changes are done. Let's verify it's actually working:

**Final check: "Can Send MMS"**

Please use the **"Can Send MMS"** action on your phone.

This will tell us whether your messaging app can send picture messages now. Let me know what it reports.

(If you'd like, you can also try resending one of the stuck photo messages directly from your messaging app — sometimes a message that's been sitting in the outbox needs to be manually resent even once everything is working.)
turns.execution_output: User: Fingers crossed — let me check.

turns.thought:
I understand — that is frustrating after all those fixes. The good news is we've ruled out the network issues, and there's one more documented cause of MMS failure we haven't checked: **app permissions**.

Your messaging app needs permission to access **storage** (for the photos) and **SMS** (to send messages). If those permissions weren't granted, picture messages will fail even with a perfect signal.

**Please use the "Check App Permissions" action for the "messaging" app.**

Let me know whether **storage** and **sms** appear in the list of granted permissions. If either is missing, I'll walk you through granting them.

(If the permissions turn out to be fine, we have a couple of other things we can look at — Data Saver mode and VPN status — so we're not out of options.)
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me check the messaging app's permissions.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's very likely the missing piece. Storage is there (so it can access your photos), but without **sms** permission the app can't actually send the message, even over a good data connection.

**Please use the "Grant App Permission" action with:**
- App: **`messaging`**
- Permission: **`sms`**

Once that's granted, please run **"Can Send MMS"** again to see if picture messaging now works.

Let me know what it reports.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, granting the SMS permission to the messaging app now.

turns.thought:
Absolutely — let's check those. I'm sorry this has taken so many steps, but we do still have things to look at.

**Please use the "Check Data Restriction Status" action.**

This shows whether **Data Saver mode** is ON or whether background data usage is restricted globally. Data Saver can throttle or block background data, which can stop picture messages from sending even with good signal.

Let me know what it reports and then we'll move on to the VPN check.

(Also worth confirming: does your status bar show a **Data Saver** icon? That would be a quick visual confirmation.)
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the data restriction status.

turns.thought:
Yes — Data Saver is off, so that's ruled out too. Let's check the VPN.

**Please use the "Check VPN Status" action.**

Let me know:
- Whether the VPN is **ON and connected**, or off
- If it is on, what the **performance level** shows

An active VPN that's slow or misconfigured can interfere with data connectivity and block picture messages from sending.

Go ahead and check that, and tell me what it says.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the VPN status.

turns.thought:
I appreciate you sticking with it — and yes, there are still a couple of things we haven't checked. Let me keep going.

Two remaining things I'd like to look at:

1. **Speed test** — this confirms whether you actually have a working data connection right now, despite the status bar showing 5G. If a speed test reports "no connection," something is still blocking data underneath.
2. **App status for "messaging"** — this shows app-specific settings, including whether **background data** is restricted for just that app. Data Saver was off globally, but the messaging app could still be restricted on its own.

Let's start with the first one.

**Please use the "Run Speed Test" action.**

Let me know what it reports — specifically whether it shows a speed (and how good) or "no connection." That will tell us whether data is genuinely flowing, and then we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me run the speed test.

turns.thought:
That's a really useful finding, and it explains a lot: your phone *thinks* it has a 5G data connection, but no data is actually flowing. That's why MMS still fails — picture messaging needs real data throughput, not just the icon.

Let me check a couple of things on your account side before we take the next step.

turns.thought:
Good question — and it's actually a very useful clue. It means your phone *thinks* it has a 5G data connection (that's why the status bar looks fine), but no data is actually flowing through. So we've fixed the radio/signal side, but something in the data connection path is still broken.

I also checked your account directly: your line **555-123-2002 is Active** with no suspension, and your bills are current — so this isn't a billing or account block. The 2 GB add-on is confirmed on your line.

The most likely remaining culprit is your **APN settings** — these control how your phone actually routes data. Earlier you read me the APN name and MMSC URL, but I'd like to see the status indicator specifically.

**Please use the "Check APN Settings" action again.**

This time, tell me:
- Does it report the settings as **"Correct"** or **"Incorrect"**?
- What APN name and MMSC URL it lists.

If it comes back "Incorrect," we'll reset them to the defaults — that plus a reboot is the standard fix and very often clears exactly this symptom (looks connected, but no data actually flows).
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the APN settings again.

turns.thought:
Understood — and that's actually helpful. Since the check doesn't report the APN as **"Incorrect"**, and both the APN name and MMSC URL are populated, the guidance I have is that resetting them isn't indicated right now. So let's hold off on that and try the other thing I flagged earlier.

Let's look at whether the messaging app itself is being restricted:

**Please use the "Check App Status" action for the "messaging" app.**

This shows app-specific details including its permissions and — importantly — whether **background data usage is restricted for this app specifically**. Data Saver was off globally, but a single app can still be restricted on its own, which would produce exactly what you're seeing: signal looks fine, but the app can't get data through.

Let me know what it reports, and whether background data shows as restricted or allowed.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the messaging app's status.

turns.thought:
Thanks — so permissions are confirmed good now (sms, storage, phone all granted), and there's no reported background data restriction. That rules out the app-level causes.

Let's try the remaining standard fix — a full restart, which refreshes all the connections and services after all the changes we've made:

**Please use the "Reboot Device" action.**

We've changed several network settings today (SIM reseat, mobile data, network mode, Wi-Fi Calling), and a reboot is the standard way to make all of those fully take effect and clear any lingering software glitch.

Once your phone is back on, please:
1. Run **"Run Speed Test"** — I want to see if data is actually flowing now.
2. Run **"Can Send MMS"** — to check picture messaging.

Let me know what those two report. If data still shows "No Connection" and MMS still fails after the reboot, then this has gone beyond what I can resolve with the tools available to me, and I'll get you over to our technical support team so they can dig in further.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me reboot the phone.

turns.thought:
I completely understand, and I'm sorry we couldn't get this resolved today — you've been really patient working through all of those steps. You're right that it's time to bring in technical support: your line is Active with no suspension and your account is current, yet data still isn't flowing even though the phone shows 5G. That points to something on the network or device level that's beyond what I can fix with my tools.

Let me transfer you now.
